1 Introduction

1.1 Purpose

This document refers to the application by its abbreviated name, TESTRX, which stands for Test Environment System for Tracking & Running Xecutions.

2 About TESTRX

2.1 Overview

TESTRX is an integrated test environment designed for test-case authoring, script generation based on test bench configurations, and test execution for validating embedded automotive systems. The tool streamlines and standardizes the entire testing workflow through a unified and intuitive interface. Key capabilities include:

Authoring test cases in a standardized and reusable format
Generating automated test scripts derived from test bench configuration parameters
Supporting a wide range of test tools and environments, including HIL systems and in-vehicle testing
Providing an intuitive graphical user interface for ease of use
Ensuring standardization of all test artifacts, including test cases, test scripts, and results
Offering a modular architecture that enables rapid customization and seamless integration with various tools in the testing ecosystem

3 TESTRX Installation and Uninstallation

The application is designed to install and uninstall seamlessly on any Windows-based system or laptop.
In the event of an installation error, the installer presents a clear notification and references the generated log file to facilitate troubleshooting.

3.1 Application Installation

The application is packaged as an MSI installer to ensure a reliable, standardized, and easily manageable deployment process across different environments.
This dual-mode installation approach enables IT administrators and end users to select the method best suited to organizational or individual requirements.

3.2 Application Uninstallation

The application may be uninstalled through any of the following methods:
Control Panel → Programs and Features
Windows Settings → Apps & Features
The uninstaller ensures system integrity by preserving shared dependencies required by other applications.
In the event of an uninstallation failure, all changes are safely rolled back and the user is informed of the issue.

4 Workspace

4.1 Workspace selection on First Launch

During the initial launch, the application automatically presents the Workspace Selection window, prompting the user to define the workspace location.
Users may specify a workspace location either by manually entering a directory path or by selecting one through the Browse option.
If the user selects “Cancel,” the operation is aborted and the application closes without storing any workspace information.

Figure Snp.1: Workspace selection

Upon confirming the workspace location by selecting “OK,” the system generates a TESTRX_Workspace directory within the chosen path and automatically creates all required subfolders.
After successful workspace configuration, the application proceeds to initialize essential components, load relevant data, and display the Test Case view.

5 Application Interface Overview

The Home screen contains the Menu Bar, Test Environment Roles Selector , Project Navigator, and Test Case Editor.

Figure Snp.2: TESTRX Home screen

The menu bar shows grouped items such as File, Edit, View, Options and Help. When clicked, each menu displays its related subcommands and actions.
The menu bar can be collapsed using the Up Arrow button. It automatically restores and becomes visible again whenever any grouped menu item is clicked.
The Home tab is the default landing page after launch and provides a quick view of project metrics, recent activity, and announcements.
The Test Case tab lets users view, create, edit, and manage test cases within the selected project or test suite.
The Test Session tab allows users to start, manage, and review test execution sessions.

6 Project Navigator

A hierarchical Project Navigator shall be displayed based on the selected user role:

Test Case Role: Displays Projects, Test Suites, and Test Cases.
Test Session Role: Displays Test Sessions, Test Suites, and Test Cases.

6.1 Navigator Panel Behaviour

When the user clicks the Test Case or Test Session tab, the Project Navigator panel shall expand to occupy the left portion of the application window, providing access to the navigation tree.
Clicking the same tab again shall collapse the Project Navigator panel and hide the tree view.

6.2 Hover and Overlay Behaviour

When the user hovers over the Test Case or Test Session tab, the Project Navigator panel shall temporarily appear as an overlay, overlapping the current content (for example, the right panel).
This behaviour provides quick access to project, test suite, and test case information without permanently occupying screen space.

6.3 Refresh, Pin and Close Controls

When the Project Navigator is displayed as an overlay, a Refresh icon shall be available which on clicked will collapse the Project Navigator panel, hiding the tree view to maximize the working area while keeping the navigator tab accessible for quick re-expansion
A Pin icon shall be available within the navigator panel, clicking the Pin icon shall lock the Project Navigator in an expanded state.
Once pinned, the navigator shall remain visible until the user manually collapses or unpins it.
A Close icon is available on the navigator panel, allowing the user to hide the Project Navigator panel from the main window.

6.4 Node Interaction

On double-clicking a selected node (for example, a Test Case or Test Suite) within the Project Navigator, a new tab shall open in the right panel.
The tab shall display detailed information or the appropriate editor view related to the selected node.

11.1 Adding Database

To add a database, click the Add(+) Icon in the upper panel of the Signia tab and select the required file type (A2L, DBC, or LDF).

Figure Snp.10: Add Function for Label Database Import

In the lower panel, use the Browse option in the Details section to locate and select the desired file, then click Save to confirm the import.
Upon saving, a confirmation message will appear indicating successful import. After acknowledging the message, the Imported On field will display the date and time of the import.
Reload option can be used to update the existing database by browsing and selecting a new or modified database file; clicking Reload re-imports the selected file and refreshes all data with the latest content.

Figure Snp.11: Reload Database File

11.2 Delete and Force Delete – Database File

These options are available in the upper panel of the Signia tab.
Allows removal of a selected database file from the Signia configuration.
The Delete option performs dependency checks and prevents removal if the file is referenced by active Test Cases.
The Force Delete option bypasses dependency validation and removes the file immediately.
The original file on the system remains unchanged; only its reference in the application is removed.
Force Delete should be used cautiously, as it overrides standard safeguards and may require updates to dependent Test Cases.

11.3 Copy and Paste – Database File

These options are available in the upper panel of the Signia tab.
The Copy option allows the selected database file to be copied from its current Test Suite.
The Paste option enables the copied database to be inserted into another Test Suite.
Only the reference within the application is duplicated; the original file on the system remains unchanged.
If the same database file is copied and attempted to be pasted into the same Test Suite, the tool displays an error message indicating that the file already exists.

11.4 Import and Export – Database File

The Import and Export options are available in the upper panel of the Signia tab.
The Import option allows users to add a database file (A2L, DBC, LDF) to the Test Suite that was exported from another test suite.
Imported files appear in the upper panel, and their details are shown in the lower panel.
If an invalid file is selected, the system displays an error message.
The Export option enables users to save the selected database file to a chosen directory.
The exported file retains all its signal information for reuse in other Test Suites.
If the export operation fails, an error popup is displayed.

12 Parameters

The Parameters feature allows users to define, manage, and apply Test Suite–level and Test Case– level parameters. Parameters support dynamic value substitution within Test Cases using the format {{parameter_name}}.

Figure Snp.12: Parameters Tab

12.1 Creating Parameters

Parameters can be created from the Parameters tab at both the Test Suite and Test Case levels, or directly within the Editor.
In the Editor, parameters are defined using the syntax {{parameter_name}}.
In the Parameters tab, new parameters can be added by selecting the ‘+’ option.
When a parameter is created through the Parameters tab, the system assigns a default name in sequential order (e.g., Parameter001, Parameter002, etc.).
Once created, the parameter row enters editable mode, allowing the user to rename and configure it immediately.
Pressing Enter confirms the parameter name and inserts it into the parameter table.
Parameters remain local to their context (Test Suite or Test Case) until explicitly saved.
Parameters can be saved by Save option in the Menu Bar or by using shortcut “Ctrl+S”

12.2 Parameter Types and Scope

12.2.1 Test Suite–Level Parameters

These parameters are global in scope and accessible across all Test Cases contained within the Test Suite.
Test Suite parameters provide default values that may be selectively overridden at the Test Case level.

12.2.2 Test Case–Level Parameters

These parameters are local to the Test Case in which they are defined.
Test Case parameters take precedence over Test Suite parameters when both share the same name.
Newly created Test Case parameters remain visible only within the specific Test Case until they are saved.

12.2.3 User-Defined Parameters

Parameters added through the editor are automatically captured and listed in the parameter table once the user confirms the input.
Multiple parameters may be entered within a single editor cell.

12.3 Parameter Naming Rules

Parameter names must adhere to strict validation rules to ensure consistency, clarity, and compatibility:

Must begin with an alphabetic character (A–Z or a–z).
May contain only alphanumeric characters and underscores (_).
Must not contain spaces.
Must be longer than three characters.
Must not begin or end with an underscore.
Must not contain consecutive underscores.
Must not be identical to reserved keywords in the target programming language.
Must not consist solely of numeric characters or numeric groups separated by underscores.

12.4 Parameter Table Structure

Each parameter includes the following fields for configuration and reference:

Name – The unique identifier of the parameter.
Description – The purpose or functional meaning of the parameter.
Value – The predefined list of acceptable values.
Current Value – The value currently assigned for use during execution.
Value Description – A detailed explanation of the selected value.
Units – Measurement units associated with the parameter value.
Set In – Indicates whether the parameter belongs to the Test Suite or Test Case.

12.5 Parameter Value Rules

12.5.1 Value Field

The Value column supports:

A single numeric value
A comma-separated list of numeric values

Validation Rules

Values must be numeric.
Duplicate values are not permitted.
Entries must be separated by commas.
No trailing or consecutive commas allowed.

Invalid Example

1,,2 or 1,2,

Valid Example

1,2,3

12.5.2 Current Value Field

The user may:

Select a value from the predefined list, or
Enter a new value manually, provided it satisfies validation rules.

Additional behaviors:

Newly entered valid values are automatically added to the Value list.
When switching between values, the corresponding Value Description and Units are preserved and reloaded.
Edits to value descriptions and units apply only to the selected value.

12.6 Renaming Parameter

Parameter names can be edited only at the Test Suite level.
If the parameter is not referenced in any Test Case, renaming occurs immediately.
If the parameter is used in one or more Test Cases, a warning dialog appears:

Parameter Warning

“The selected parameter is already used in Test Case!” To rename from old_param to new_param, click Continue. To add it as a new parameter, click Create New.”

All naming rules are revalidated before finalizing the rename.

12.7 Removing Parameters

A right-click on a parameter row in the parameter tab opens the context menu with Remove Parameter.
Removal is confirmed via popup: Confirm deletion of the parameter “parameter_name”?
Deletion occurs only after user confirmation.

13 Labels

The Labels tab is displayed on the right side of the interface, similar to the Details tab, and is available exclusively at the Test Suite level. This tab provides a consolidated view of all labels referenced across the Test Cases within the current Test Suite.

Figure Snp.13: Labels Tab

13.1 Label Availability and Creation

The Labels tab lists all labels used in any Test Case under the selected Test Suite.
Users may create new labels within the Test

view of all labels referenced across the Test Cases within the current Test Suite.

Figure Snp.13: Labels Tab

13.1 Label Availability and Creation

The Labels tab lists all labels used in any Test Case under the selected Test Suite.
Users may create new labels within the Test Case editor by entering them in appropriate column Identifier.
Newly created labels become available in the Labels tab only after the user saves the changes.
Saved labels are made globally accessible across all Test Suites, ensuring consistency and centralized management.

13.2 Labels Tab Columns

The Labels tab displays the following columns:

Name – Displays the label name referenced within the Test Cases. This is the only field that can be modified by the user.
Default Value – Shows the default value fetched from the associated database file (A2L, DBC, LDF). This value is system-derived and not user-editable.
Factor – Represents the scaling factor applied to the raw signal value; automatically populated from the imported metadata.
Offset – Indicates the offset used in signal conversion calculations; auto-filled based on the label’s source definition.
Units – Specifies the measurement units associated with the label (e.g., °C, km/h), derived automatically from metadata.
Min Value – Displays the minimum permissible value for the label as defined in the source file.
Max Value – Displays the maximum permissible value for the label as defined in the source file.
Data Type – Indicates the data type of the label (e.g., uint8, float, int16), determined from the imported database.
Description – Provides a brief explanation or meaning of the label, populated from available metadata in the source file.

13.3 Label Management Options

13.3.1 Remove Label

Users can remove labels directly from the Labels tab.
If a label is referenced in any Test Case, the system prevents removal and displays a warning: "Cannot remove label as it is used in Test Case(s)."

13.3.2 Renaming Labels

When a user attempts to rename a label:

If the new name already exists within the same Test Case or Test Suite, the system shows a confirmation popup: "A label with the name '<new_name>' already exists. Do you want to merge the current label with the existing one?"
Yes → The system merges all associated reference data into the existing label.
Cancel → The rename is aborted with no changes applied.

A Test Case can be created in two ways:

Right-click the desired Test Suite or Test Case and select Add Test Case or Add

Heading.

Use the New menu, which provides two options—Test Case and Heading—and

select the desired option to create.

A new node is inserted into the selected Test Suite/Test Case and opened in inline edit mode.

14.1 Naming Rules

A Test Case name may include letters, numbers, spaces, and the underscore (_).
The system enforces the following:
Name cannot be empty → “Case name cannot be empty.”
Maximum length: 150 characters
Cannot begin with a special character
Leading/trailing spaces are trimmed automatically
Invalid characters are not allowed: , : * ? " < > | @ # $ etc.
Reserved terms may be restricted (e.g., default, null, system) → “The name uses a reserved keyword. Please choose a different name.”
Pressing Enter confirms the name and saves the Test Case.

14.3 Test Case Editor – Sequence Tab

The Sequence tab becomes available when a test case is selected and is displayed in the rightside panel. This tab allows users to edit the test case, including modifying steps and configurations.

Figure Snp.15: Test Case Editor

The Sequence tab displays a fixed-layout table organized into three distinct sections, each identified by a labelled header:
Setup: Defines the automated preconditions and initialization steps required before test execution, such as environment configuration, data preparation, and system setup.
Sequence: Contains the automated test steps that drive the core execution logic, including actions, validations, and control flow.
Shut Down: Specifies automated clean-up activities and post-execution validations, such as resource release, log collection, and system reset.
The following columns are available for defining each test step:
Instruction: Defines the automated action to be executed as part of the test step (e.g., Set, Check ,While).
Entity Type: Specifies the type of component the instruction acts upon (e.g., CAN Signal, Ethernet Message).
Identifier: Represents the user defined label or parameter used to configure the entity
Control Logic: Defines the conditional logic governing the execution of the step (e.g., Expected Vale is >20 with tolerance of 1%).
Annotation: Allows users to add comments or descriptive notes for documentation, clarity, or maintenance purposes (e.g., Validates successful login, Precondition: Application is launched).

Remove Step(s) | Deletes the selected step(s) from the test case.
Convert Step ↔ Nested Step | Converts a step to a nested step or a nested step to a normal step.
Copy Step(s) | Copies the selected step(s) to the clipboard.
Cut Steps(s) | Cuts the selected step(s) and places them on the clipboard.
Paste Step(s) | Pastes the copied or cut step(s) at the selected location.

14.6 Identifier

The Identifier field is a text input with autocomplete support that allows users to select or define the specific object targeted in a test step.
The suggestion list is dynamically filtered based on the selected Entity Type.
Users can type to search existing identifiers or enter a new identifier if it does not already exist (for example, a signal name, variable, or parameter).
This field is used to precisely identify the message, signal, variable, or parameter that the test step will act upon.

14.7 Control Logic

The Control Logic window allows users to define conditions, references, and timing constraints that control how an automated test step is executed and evaluated. This logic determines whether a step should pass, fail, or wait based on defined criteria. The clear option clears only the updated or modified values of the existing control logic and restores the previously saved configuration.

Figure Snp.16: Edit Control Logic Window

14.7.1 Value

The Value section is used to define the expected value or condition that must be satisfied during automated execution.
Users can select the data type (for example, String or numeric type) and enter the expected value.
A comparison operator can be selected to evaluate the actual runtime value against the expected value.
Tolerance and unit fields allow flexibility in value comparison, supporting range-based validation.
This condition is evaluated automatically during test execution.

14.7.2 Reference Step

The Reference Step section allows the current step to be evaluated based on the result of another step in the test sequence.
Users can select a previously defined step as a reference.
The Verdict field specifies the expected result of the referenced step (for example, Pass).
During automation, the current step is executed or validated only if the referenced step meets the defined verdict.

14.7.3 Time Constraint

The Time Constraint section defines timing rules for automated execution.
The Mode field specifies how timing should be applied (for example, timeout or delay).
The Time field defines the duration for which the automation should wait or monitor the condition
Tolerance allows minor timing variations without causing test failure.
This ensures synchronization and reliable execution in time-dependent scenarios.
There are 4 modes in time that was described below :
After: The condition is considered valid only when it occurs after the acceptable range. With tolerance applied, the condition may be accepted even if it occurs slightly before the end of the acceptable range, or within a defined early tolerance window.
Before: The condition is considered valid only when it occurs before the acceptable range. When tolerance is enabled, the condition may still be treated as valid if it slightly overlaps into the beginning of the acceptable range, within the defined tolerance limits.
In Range: The condition is considered valid when it occurs within the acceptable range. Depending on the configuration, limited tolerance may allow the condition to be satisfied slightly before the start of the range (early hit), slightly after the end of the range (late hit), or on both sides. If no tolerance is applied, the condition must strictly stay within the defined range.
Entire Range: The condition is same as In Range but

range (early hit), slightly after the end of the range (late hit), or on both sides. If no tolerance is applied, the condition must strictly stay within the defined range.
Entire Range: The condition is same as In Range but the difference is that the value should occur in the entire time range. The condition is considered valid when it occurs anywhere within the acceptable range. When tolerance is enabled, the condition may also be accepted if it occurs slightly before or slightly after the acceptable range, as long as it remains within the configured tolerance boundaries.
Example of Time Constraint: In the below image the condition is evaluated over the entire time range from 5 to 10 seconds. With Early Hit and Late enabled and a tolerance of ±1 second, the condition is accepted if it occurs between 4 and 11 seconds.

Figure Snp.17: Time Constraint Example

14.7.4 Range of Steps

This control logic is available only when the “When” action is selected in the instruction and is used to evaluate conditions over a specified range of previously authored steps.
For example, if the range is set from step 1 to step 2, the conditions defined in the While logic are continuously checked during the execution of steps 1 through 2.
In the tool, this range is displayed as “From Setup Step 1 to Setup Step 2”, indicating that the condition is evaluated during the execution of those setup steps.

Figure Snp.18: Range of Steps for While

This range of steps is also available when the Repeat action is selected.
When Repeat is enabled, additional automation logic is provided to control how the steps are repeated:  Condition defines the criteria that must be satisfied for the repeat execution to continue.  Count specifies the maximum number of times the selected range of steps should be executed.  Duration specifies the maximum time for which the selected range of steps should be repeated, after which the repeat execution stops.
The selected setup steps from Setup Step 1 to Setup Step 3 are executed repeatedly. The repetition continues until the defined condition is met and is controlled by duration, meaning the steps will keep repeating for 5 ms, after which the execution stops automatically.

Figure Snp.19: Range of Steps for Repeat

Once test cases are authored in the Test Case tab, they must go through the following execution workflow:

Test Bench Configuration setup
Define and configure a Test Plan
Execute the configured test cases

This structured process ensures controlled planning, traceability, and systematic execution of test cases within the application.

16.1 Link Test Cases with a Test Session

This section describes the procedure for associating test cases with a test session to enable execution and tracking. To view the test steps in Test Session or Test Plan click on the ID column of that particular test case.

16.1.1 Select a Project and Create a Test Session

From the File menu, select New and hover over Select Project. The system displays all projects available in the Test Case tab. Select the required project to add it to the workspace.
After the project is added, select the project node right click and choose Add Test Session. Alternatively, a test session can be created by selecting Test Session from the New option in the File menu.

16.1.2 Link Test Suites and Add Test Cases

Once the test session is created, right-click the test session and select Link to Test Suite. The system displays a list of all available test suites. Select the appropriate test suite.

After a test suite is selected, the Test Cases panel is displayed on the right side, listing all test cases associated with the selected test suite.
Expand the test suite using the arrow icon to view individual test cases. Drag and drop the required test cases into the test session to include them for execution.
When a nested test case is collapsed and dragged into a test session, all its child test cases are automatically included in the test session.
To include test cases from additional test suites, repeat the same procedure by linking the required test suite to the test session.

Figure Snp.24: Window for drag and drop of test cases

16.2.3 Configurator Tab – Toolbar Options

The Configurator tab provides a set of toolbar actions that allow users to efficiently manage Test Bench Configuration (TBC) items. These options are available in the upper panel of the Configurator tab and support standard configuration management activities.

Figure Snp.32: Configurator Tool bar

The following actions are available:

Add: Adds a new item, such as a Test Bench Configuration (TBC) or an interface, under the selected node.
Enable TBC: Enables the selected TBC node for execution.
Delete: Deletes the selected TBC node from the configurator.
Copy: Creates a duplicate of the selected configuration item for reuse.
Paste: Pastes the copied configuration item into the selected location within the configurator hierarchy.
Import: Imports a previously exported TBC ZIP file into the configurator.
Export: Exports the selected TBC as a ZIP file for backup or reuse.

16.2.4 Map Labels

The Map Labels option is available only for TBC nodes in the project tree.
Selecting this option opens the Map Labels window, allowing users to view, edit, import, export, and save label mappings.
The Map Labels Window provides a centralized interface for configuring and managing label-tosignal mappings used during test execution.
It allows users to map logical labels defined in test cases to their corresponding database signals, ensuring correct read/write and diagnostic communication during execution.

Figure Snp.33: Map Labels Window

16.2.4.1 Overview

The Map Labels window consists of two main tabs: Test Labels IO Labels
The Test Labels tab is displayed by default when the window is opened.
Common action buttons — Autofill, Import, Export, Cancel, and Save — are available at the bottom of the window.
A details panel is displayed below the grid to show additional read/write path information for the selected label.
The Dependencies option allows users to add dependency labels when required. If no dependencies are needed, this option can be disabled.

16.2.4.2 Test Labels Tab

The Test Labels tab displays all labels used in the current test session. These labels are automatically extracted from the test cases linked to the active test session.
This tab enables mapping of test labels to their corresponding Read Path and Write Path sourced from the active CANoe database.
The tab is divided into two vertically stacked sections:
Test Label Mapping Grid (Upper Section): The grid automatically lists all test labels used in the active test session. Labels are dynamically collected by analysing all test cases and extracting label definitions from their Labels objects.

16.2.4.3 IO Labels Tab

The IO Labels tab provides a unified interface for mapping all user-defined input/output labels to database Read and Write paths. These labels represent hardware or external interfaces used during test execution.
The tab consists of two sections:
I/O Mapping Grid (Upper Section): Displays all IO labels extracted from the test session, with editable Read and Write path mappings. Invalid or missing signal mappings are highlighted visually to indicate configuration issues.
Mapping Details Panel (Lower Section): Displays tool interface details, file references, and mapping information for the selected IO label. All fields in this section are non-editable and update automatically based on grid selection.

16.2.4.4 Autofill Functionality

The Autofill option automatically populates Read and Write paths across all three tabs — Test Labels, IO Labels, and Diagnostics — by matching label names with available signals from connected CANoe databases.

16.2.4.5 Import and Export

The Import option is used to load label mapping data for all tabs from a ZIP file. If mapping data already exists, a confirmation is displayed before replacing the current mappings.
The Export option is used to save the current label mappings from all tabs into a ZIP file. The export operation does not affect the existing mappings in the workspace.

16.2.4.6 Label Validation and Visual Indicators

Labels with missing or invalid database signals are highlighted in pink.
Read/Write dropdowns are disabled when valid signals are unavailable.
All dropdowns display full hierarchical signal names and refresh automatically when the database or configuration changes.

17 JAMA Integration

Jama is an Application Lifecycle Management (ALM) tool used to manage requirements, test cases, and traceability. The JAMA Integration enables automation-based synchronization between the test automation framework and Jama Connect, ensuring consistent and up-to-date test artifacts.

17.1 Test Case Role

In the Test Case role, users can automate interactions with ALM to manage test projects, test suites, and test cases. This role supports loading projects from ALM, synchronizing automated test updates, and maintaining requirement traceability.

Key functionalities include:

Loading of test projects from ALM
Flushing modified test suites and test cases back to ALM
Linking requirements to test cases through the Traceability tab

17.1.1 Load Project from ALM

To load a project from ALM, navigate to File → New → Project and select the Load option.

Figure Snp.41: Load option for project

Enter valid ALM credentials and click Submit.

Figure Snp.42: Authentication Window

The Load Project window is displayed. Select the required project from the drop-down list and click OK. The selected project is then loaded into the automation environment.
After loading, double-click the project to view all available test suites associated with it. To load a specific test suite, select the required test suite from the list, right-click, and choose Load Test Suite.

Figure Snp.43: Load Test Suite Option

Provide valid credentials when prompted. The selected test suite is then loaded and becomes available for automation and execution.

17.1.2 Flush Modified Test Suites and Test Cases

If any modifications are made to test suites or test cases that were loaded from ALM, those changes can be synchronized back to ALM using the Flush operation.
To flush updates, select the modified test suite or test case and navigate to File → Flush. Enter valid ALM credentials and click Submit.

Figure Snp.44: Flush Menu Option

The flushing progress and status are displayed in a notification tooltip at the top-right corner of the application. Options to minimize or close the notification are also available.

Note

Only test suites and test cases that were originally loaded from ALM are eligible for flushing.

To link requirements to a test case, double-click the required test case to open its details view. Navigate to the Traceability tab located on the right side of the screen.
Within the Traceability table, right-click on the S.No cell and select Add Requirement. Enter the corresponding ALM

requirements to a test case, double-click the required test case to open its details view. Navigate to the Traceability tab located on the right side of the screen.
